legend.ects: Workload in ECTS credits; 1 ECTS credit is about 25 hours of work.

assessment.final: Assessed at the end of the course (exam).

types.EX: Not defined in the source legend

courses.title: Audience Engagement
courses.content: Audience Engagement in Audiovisual Media: From Traditional to Interactive This course examines the concept of audience engagement in the context of audiovisual media. It will analyze the different ways in which audiences interact with media, including attention, interest, and participation. Various strategies that media creators can use to foster engagement across different media formats will be explored. Audience Engagement: Engagement compared to Attention, Interest, and Participation Different techniques used by media producers to create engaging content will be examined, including narrative structure, character development, and visual design. Examples from traditional media will be analyzed, and the strategies used to generate engagement will be investigated. Interactive media, such as video games and immersive experiences, offer unique opportunities for audience engagement. The course will explore the various ways interactive media captivate audiences, including player interaction, immersive storytelling, and social gaming. In the digital media landscape, audiences are often active on multiple platforms (multi-platform engagement) and across various media formats. Strategies for creating a cohesive and engaging experience across different platforms, including social media, web-sites, and mobile apps, will be examined.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to understand the concept of audience engagement in the context of audiovisual media. They can distinguish between engagement, attention, interest, and participation, and analyze the strategies used by media creators to foster audience engagement across different media formats. They are also able to apply this knowledge to their own media projects.

courses.title: Impulse
courses.content: A lecture series featuring various presentations from different disciplines and speakers. The goal is to introduce diverse ways of thinking and approaches, utilizing a wide range of forms of expression, in order to showcase the broad scope of possible topics.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply in-depth knowledge of cutting-edge multimedia projects and current research in the areas of the Creative Industries, such as Art-Based Research, Playable Media, Audiovisual Environments, Film, Communication and Crossmedia Design, and Interaction Design. In addition, they develop creative and artistic master’s project topics and communicate the program’s quality expectations regarding these projects.

courses.title: Impulse Workshops
courses.content: A workshop series featuring various disciplines and different presenters. The goal is to introduce diverse ways of thinking and approaches, using a wide range of forms of expression, in order to showcase the broad scope of possible topics.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to identify relevant topics for a master’s project through inspiration, research, and analysis. They can find problems and research questions related to a potential creative-artistic master’s project, with a focus on multimedia platforms in the constantly evolving forms of communication and technologies. Furthermore, they are able to write short concepts or exposés for the applicable fields.

courses.title: Master Project - Development - Presentation
courses.content: Advanced knowledge and skills to present the preliminary concept of the chosen master's project to potential clients, team members, or supervisors. This includes outlining the relevance, the problem statement, research questions related to both the work and theory, as well as presenting potential solutions. Enhanced competence to take on a responsible role within a project team. This involves introducing the team and presenting the resource planning.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to present their project to team members and supervisors. They can communicate the relevance, problem statement, and proposed solutions clearly and take on a responsible role and function within a team.

courses.title: Media Studies 1
courses.content: The analysis of media phenomena through everyday media applications is the focus of this lecture. Semiotic, phenomenological, and discursive methods will be introduced, and the insights gained from these analyses will be placed within broader theoretical contexts to highlight fundamental characteristics of media cultures (or cultures constructed by media) of the 20th and 21st centuries. The lecture will address awareness of media epochs and their shifts, as well as the differences and repetitions, alongside a critical engagement with media manipulation and ethical questions, such as those posed by artificial intelligence. Key Topics: ’ Theories of media and their analysis (discourse, content, framing, semiotics, reception) ’ The power of media (industries) and their impact on culture and society ’ Global media and cultural imperialism ’ Stereotypes and representation ’ Selected positions in Gender and Queer Studies ’ Media activism and social change
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to use methods from media studies to scientifically contextualize current media transformations and critically reflect on their own aesthetic and creative processes. They can convey theories in a way that allows them to be applied to their respective master’s theses and generate ideas for topics and hypotheses for their master’s projects.

courses.title: Peer Presentation 1: Show & Tell
courses.content: Students are the focal point, presenting and discussing the various cultural, media, and artistic influences that have shaped and inspired their creative work. Through a series of 10-minute presentations, students will shed light on their personal experiences and artistic backgrounds, highlighting the different aspects that contribute to their unique styles and perspectives. Each participant will present their own creative journey and provide insights into how various elements from culture, media, and art have influenced their work. By engaging with a wide range of sources of inspiration, including literature, films, music, visual arts, and traditional cultural practices, students will develop a deeper understanding of the interplay between artistic disciplines and cultural influences.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to reflect on their own artistic processes and identify key cultural, media, and artistic influences that have shaped their work. They recognize the diversity of perspectives and influences among their peers, inspiring them to explore new directions in their own creative practice. Furthermore, they engage in thoughtful discussions and exchange ideas with their peers, fostering a collaborative learning environment. Finally, they demonstrate a deeper understanding of various cultures, media, and art forms and their influence on creative work.

courses.title: Positions on Art & Media Culture
courses.content: The lecture will explore contemporary art influences and positions, highlighting various aspects in the context of new media. Through audiovisual examples from fine art, popular, and digital art, it will contextualize and discuss the shifts and influences of the 20th and 21st centuries, from the Surrealists to multimedia productions. The impact of media and how artists use these platforms to create and share their work will also be addressed, as well as the reception of current art productions with regard to the students' master's projects.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop a comprehensive understanding of artistic productions and their integration into media cultures and classical art movements. They work with tools that allow them to critically analyze the ever-changing landscape of art and media culture and to reflect on it within their own creative work.

courses.title: Symposium: Ethics & Sustainability
courses.content: Fundamental knowledge of career-related discourses on ethics and sustainability in the context of health and social care, information technologies, wood and biogenic technologies, media and design, as well as business and tourism, will be conveyed during the symposium, with varying thematic focuses.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates acquire the competence to analyze, evaluate, argue, and reflect on relevant contexts. They are able to integrate these into their own sustainable and responsible courses of action.

courses.title: Master Project - Development - AUDIOVISUAL ENVIRONMENTS
courses.content: Developing differentiated skills in creating solutions for formulated problems and research questions. Refining and shaping (creatively/theoretically/scientifically; based on the state of the art) the skill, to transfer a concept into a project. Development of a pre-liminary concept for the master's project. Team formation and resource planning.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to transition the basic concept of their master’s project into the pre-production phase. They can assemble a team for project execution and develop a resource plan for the project.

courses.title: Master Project - Development - COMMUNICATION DESIGN
courses.content: Developing differentiated skills in creating solutions for formulated problems and research questions. Refining and shaping (creatively/theoretically/scientifically; based on the state of the art) the skill, to transfer a concept into a project. Development of a pre-liminary concept for the master's project. Team formation and resource planning.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to transition the basic concept of their master’s project into the pre-production phase. They can assemble a team for project execution and develop a resource plan for its implementation.

courses.title: Master Project - Development - FILM
courses.content: Developing differentiated skills in creating solutions for formulated problems and research questions. Refining and shaping (creatively/theoretically/scientifically; based on the state of the art) the skill, to transfer a concept into a project. Development of a pre-liminary concept for the master's project. Team formation and resource planning.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to transition the basic concept of their master’s project into the pre-production phase. They can assemble a team for project execution and develop a resource plan for the project’s implementation.

courses.title: Audio Masterclass 1: Music Production & Live Performance Topics
courses.content: The guest professor from the field of audio brings in industry-relevant, socially perti-nent, and/or artistically current topics and insights. Emerging technologies, such as generative sound design, are also addressed.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to incorporate their knowledge of industry-relevant, socially pertinent, and/or artistically current topics and trends into their work.

courses.title: Film Scoring & Music Production
courses.content: Score Direction and Producing (International Connections) Score and Source Music Concepts Current Trends and Artistic Impact Composition, Arrangement & Notation Sound Aesthetics & Analysis Experimental Scoring Music Sound Design Advanced Sound Synthesis International Connections Artistic-Creative Practice and Semester Project
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to identify and create current sound-aesthetic concepts in music production. They explore and experiment with new musical sound aesthetics, recognize image-based linear composition and creative-artistic music direction. Furthermore, they develop the module semester project and incorporate the learned concepts into the design and conception of the master’s project.

courses.title: Sound Design, Sound Art & Mix
courses.content: Sound Aesthetics Recording Arts: Ambient, Field Recording & Foley Sound Modification & Sound Art Music Sound Design Experimental Sound Design Speech Modification Multichannel Audio Automation Concepts Re-Recording, Film Mixing Artistic-Creative Practice and Semester Project
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop current sound-aesthetic concepts for sound design in music and gain knowledge of contemporary sound aesthetics in the field of multimedia. They can execute image-based, linear sound design as well as creative-artistic sound design direction. Graduates integrate the acquired knowledge into the conception and design of their master’s project.

courses.title: Experiment & Strategy
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Focusing Communication Design
courses.content: Advanced knowledge and skills in the systematic exploration and application of forms of expression using digital, visual, tactile, and/or multisensory design techniques, as well as the development of unconventional ideas related to a semester theme.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to systematically step out of their creative comfort zones and create a new quality of visual languages, using both digital and analogue methods. From the resulting variety of possibilities, they make strategic decisions for communicating the overarching theme, taking into account both human-centered and business-oriented approaches.

courses.title: Experimental Typography
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Focusing Communication Design
courses.content: Design techniques for recognizing, questioning, and overcoming one's own creative habits. The diversity of typographic possibilities is methodically explored to the limits of legibility. In the process, attention to one's own working methods is refined, and new perspectives are gained.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply learned methods to their own creative practices. They can recognize, question, and overcome these methods in order to develop new and diverse variations.

courses.title: CineCraft Transmedia Narrative 1
courses.content: Development of larger narrative arcs and experimentation with classic cinematic storytelling patterns, character and plot development. Further development of traditional storytelling structures towards cross-transmedia narrative arcs that integrate various media formats. Transmedia formats as well as fusion formats like film and games, along with the integration of Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), and Extended Reality (XR). These approaches make it possible to present narrative content in innovative and immersive ways, engaging audiences across different platforms and media.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to use cross-platform storytelling, telling stories seamlessly across various media and platforms. They can create cross-media narrative strategies that integrate multiple media formats. Furthermore, they apply AI-supported storytelling methods to enhance narrative development and improve efficiency. In addition, they utilize innovative media integration to create immersive and forward-looking narrative experiences.

courses.title: CineTech Innovation Masterclass 1
courses.content: Focus on the integration of the latest technologies from digital moving image production. Deepening knowledge of cutting-edge technological developments such as Virtual Production and other emerging technologies in the field of moving images. New digital production formats like Virtual Production and AI tools will be included in the course content as needed, to provide a closer understanding of these technologies and to ensure staying up-to-date with the latest technological advancements.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to integrate the latest technologies from digital moving image production. They can apply and further explore emerging technologies in the moving image sector, such as Virtual Production. In addition, they utilize new digital production formats like Virtual Production and AI tools. Graduates are able to adapt and apply these technologies in educational contexts as needed. They also continuously update their knowledge of technological developments, engage technically with the latest innovations, and develop innovative and interactive production formats.

courses.title: CineTech Preproduction Mastery 1
courses.content: Skills in using new AI tools and digital technologies for creating previsualizations and innovative formats are deepened in this course, enhancing participants' knowledge and abilities in applying these technologies for narrative development. The focus is on expanding classic storytelling structures towards cross-platform and cross-media storytelling, as well as the previsualization and visual preproduction of more complex narrative structures and challenging cross-media formats. Additionally, the course supports the development of innovative format ideas, along with their previsualization and visual preproduction.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop and integrate complex cross-platform narrative structures. They implement cross-media storytelling and create previsualizations of more complex narrative structures for Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), and Extended Reality (XR) in narrative projects. Furthermore, they support the development of innovative format ideas and integrate new technological advancements to create immersive and interactive experiences. They plan, previsualize, and present their concepts in ways that engage and interact with audiences across various platforms.

courses.title: DoP 1 Masterclass
courses.content: Advanced analytical, optimization, integration, and problem-solving skills for handling complex lighting and camera-related challenges in intricate scenarios, project work-flows, and process options. Focused planning knowledge and execution skills in lighting and camera workflows aligned with the latest technological advancements. Refined artistic, aesthetic, and organizational skills in camera and lighting work across various genres in a cross-platform context. The focus is on the use of profes-sional lighting and camera technology for complex scenarios, especially in multime-dia and special effects-heavy film productions.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to understand the complex workflow of a digital cinema camera (ARRI Alexa/Amira). They can create lighting setups and manage complex lighting situations and concepts. Furthermore, they use the camera as a means of artistic expression and integrate themselves effectively into a complex digital cinema production team. In addition, they think beyond traditional platforms and experiment with new artistic formats and technologies.

courses.title: Creative Business: Budgeting
courses.content: In this course, students will learn the key concepts and principles of budgeting and financial calculation for creative projects. They will be introduced to various methods and estimation techniques used in the industry to estimate time and costs for different media productions. Students will also learn how to identify and address common budgeting challenges, such as managing project scope, optimizing resource allocation, and ensuring financial sustainability. Additionally, the importance of effective team acquisition, personnel management, and decision-making in the budgeting process will be emphasized.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to understand and apply the key principles and methods of budgeting and financial calculation for creative projects. They develop collaboration skills and apply them in meetings to foster creativity and innovation. In addition, they can estimate time and costs for various media productions using different estimation methods and acquire the skills needed to prepare for meetings in the creative industry to ensure they are effective and time-efficient. Furthermore, they are capable of identifying and addressing common challenges in planning creative projects and making informed decisions regarding resource allocation and the financial sustainability of creative projects.

courses.title: Managing the Creative Process
courses.content: The course covers the process of developing and refining creative concepts, from the initial idea to the finished, polished product. Students will learn methods for idea generation, such as brainstorming, 6 Sigma, crazy 8s, and mind mapping, as well as techniques for concept development and iteration. The lecture will also address the importance of human-centered design principles in the creative process, with a focus on user research and feedback. Students will learn about the challenges and potential obstacles that may arise during the creative process and how to effectively overcome them. Finally, the lecture will discuss success criteria for evaluating the quality of a creative concept and explore strategies for further refining the concept.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply idea generation methods such as brainstorming and mind mapping to create creative ideas. They use concept development and iteration techniques to refine their concepts and enhance their quality. In addition, they understand the importance of human-centered design principles in the creative process and know how to conduct effective user research and feedback. They can identify potential challenges and obstacles that may arise during the creative process and learn how to effectively overcome them. Finally, they are able to evaluate the quality of a creative concept and develop strategies to further refine it.

courses.title: Media Law 1
courses.content: In this lecture, the legal foundations and contractual agreements in the creative industries will be thoroughly discussed. Students will become familiar with the legal frameworks that are crucial for the creation of software, games, music, film, and other forms of entertainment. Additionally, students will explore the various types of contracts used in the entertainment industry, such as talent contracts, licensing agreements, and production contracts. The course will also address the key legal challenges faced by industry professionals, including intellectual property rights, copyright infringement, and contract disputes.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to recognize and explain the legal foundations of the creative industries. They can analyze and evaluate contracts commonly used in the creative industries and identify and assess legal issues that frequently arise in the entertainment industry. Furthermore, they apply legal principles to hypothetical scenarios in the entertainment industry and discuss the ethical implications of legal decisions in this field.

courses.title: Meetings & Moderation
courses.content: In this course, various strategies and methods for conducting effective meetings in the creative industry will be covered. The importance of preparation, collaboration, and feedback for the success of meetings will be discussed, along with how effective facilitation can impact professional success. We will also explore the business relevance of effective meetings and moderation in the creative economy. This lecture provides students with practical skills and knowledge to conduct effective meetings, which they can apply in their professional careers.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to identify various strategies and methods that can be used to conduct effective meetings in the creative industry. They develop collaboration skills and apply them in meetings to foster creativity and innovation. Furthermore, they understand the relevance of feedback and how it can be used to improve meeting outcomes.

courses.title: Production Management Methods 1
courses.content: This course provides students with an overview of various project management (PM) methods, including Agile, Kanban, Scrum, and Waterfall (film production, campaigns, etc.). The course reviews the fundamentals of project management and introduces students to the essential concepts of each PM method, including the roles and responsibilities of project team members, the phases of a project, and the tools and techniques used to manage and monitor projects. Additionally, the course addresses the importance of selecting the right project management method for a specific project based on its unique characteristics and requirements. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the fundamentals of project management and the PM methods commonly used in the industry.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to explain the key principles of the project management methods Agile, Kanban, Scrum, and Waterfall. They can describe the roles and responsibilities of project team members in each methodology and identify the phases of a project as well as the tools and methods used to manage and monitor project progress in each project management method. Furthermore, they evaluate project characteristics and requirements to select the appropriate PM method for a specific project. Finally, they are able to apply the various PM methods covered in the lecture and create a corresponding project setup.

courses.title: Art Based Research
courses.content: Art-Based Research focuses on the use of art as a research method across various disciplines. Students learn how to apply artistic practices and methods to investigate research questions, analyze and interpret artworks as data, and utilize artistic presentations as research outcomes. The course also addresses ethical issues related to the use of art in research and explores the relationship between art and science. Course topics: * Introduction to art-based research and its applications * Art and research questions: Methods and approaches * Artworks as data: Analysis and interpretation * Art and knowledge: Theories of art and science * Artistic presentations: Expressing research findings * Ethics in art-based research * Art, science, and society: The role of art in research and society * The relationship between art and science: Collaboration and conflict
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to conduct an in-depth study of a specific topic or problem by combining artistic practice and research methods. They critically reflect on their own artistic practice and that of others, formulate research questions, and select appropriate methods for data collection and analysis. They present and publish their findings in a clear and compelling manner by using suitable artistic forms and techniques. Furthermore, they develop an understanding of how art-based research can be used as a method to explore and discuss relevant social, cultural, and political issues.

courses.title: Intercultural Competence
courses.content: In this course, various theoretical concepts related to cultural diversity are introduced, with approaches and models for communication and collaboration discussed, along with the reflection of (personal) experiences. Initially, fundamental questions, definitions, and theories regarding communication, culture, cultural codes and standardizations, identity, nationality, trans- and interculturality, diversity, and inclusion will be covered. In the later stages, key topics will be explored and presented through case studies and exercises. The goal of the course is to equip students with knowledge of how to navigate cultural differences and their impact on communication and collaboration within diverse cultural contexts.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates develop a deep understanding of intercultural interactions and the underlying communication theories, as well as critically reflect on their own cultural identities and biases. They cultivate an awareness of the importance of intercultural competence and sensitivity to stereotyping in various professional fields of art, culture, and the creative industries.

courses.title: Media Studies 2
courses.content: Students will gain in-depth insights into the following topics: the impact of digital media on society, transnational media phenomena and cultural hybridity, global media economy, identity, politics, and the public sphere. Issues of media ethics, responsibility, and censorship in media productions will be critically examined and contextualized in relation to students' own work and current examples from the media landscape. Key topics include: * Digital media and its impact on society * Globalization, transnational media, and cultural hybridity * Media and identity constructions regarding gender, race, and class * Media ethics and regulation, responsibility, and censorship in media
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to contextualize current media transformations scientifically using methods from media studies and critically reflect on their aesthetic and creative processes. They can apply theories to their master’s theses and generate ideas for topics and hypotheses for their master’s projects.

courses.title: Research Methods & Study Design
courses.content: Continuous guidance in the independent handling of a complex problem based on scientific and methodological approaches. Selected qualitative and quantitative research methods are introduced and serve as the foundation for developing a proposal for the master's thesis and the central research question. Students will develop their own scientific topics within the course, present them, and engage in academic discourse with their peer group.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates understand qualitative and quantitative research methods as well as the common procedures for developing a master’s thesis at an advanced level. They are able to create a proposal (exposé) that includes a research question, planned research design, primary sources, and an optional connection to the master’s project.

courses.title: Master Project - Conception - AUDIOVISUAL ENVIRONMENTS
courses.content: Group Project-Based Coaching: Expanding knowledge of methods in staging, workflows, and processes, as well as the practical, theoretical, and artistic approaches behind them, along with projectspecific input. Historical and critical examination of significant projects in the commercial and artistic fields. The course stimulates the collaborative development of visions within interdisciplinary group settings, exploring the boundaries of possible application areas and ultimately converging on a shared core theme or project, which is then presented through creative artistic abstraction.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop concepts, resource plans, and budgets, and to execute ambitious and creative audiovisual environment projects using state-of-the-art technology. Where necessary, they can also implement the development and integration of programming environments and/or interactive musical/sound design. Furthermore, they create concept development guided by thematic motifs for project orientation, such as sound, impact, and evolutionary, psychological, and cultural effects and approaches.

courses.title: Master Project - Conception - COMMUNICATION DESIGN
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 1 - Refined Concept - Communication Design
courses.content: Based on the students' concepts, subject-specific questions in communication design will be discussed. The focus is on the context of the master’s projects in the context of historical change and international competition, as well as the development of clear communication goals and strategies.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to recognize common methods for researching and planning communication design projects. They define communication goals and strategies for the master’s project and present initial ideas for implementation.

courses.title: Master Project - Conception - FILM
courses.content: Expanding knowledge of the culture, projects, methods, workflows, and processes of innovative cinema projects (FutureCinema), as well as the theoretical, artistic, and practical approaches behind them. The boundaries of traditional cinema are explored and deliberately surpassed. Starting with the classic screen and TV films with more or less linear storytelling, the course breaks the limits of format and genre, discovering new ways of cinematic storytelling and cross-media communication. Platforms such as pho-tography, architecture, theater, games, the internet, artistic installations, and print intersect, giving cinema a new face. Specific knowledge and skills in the conceptualization, resource planning, budgeting, and execution of ambitious and creative film projects using the latest technology, as well as the development of detailed project concepts. Refined competencies in developing shared visions within interdisciplinary teams that push the boundaries of the application field. Independent creation of film concepts.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to incorporate their ideas from the impulse workshops and the Script Development course and further develop them in an interdisciplinary manner with a focus on the larger master’s project. They shape the idea into initial forms that include the option of feasibility. Furthermore, they integrate interdisciplinary, conceptual, and technological input into the further development of the implementable idea.

courses.title: Audio Masterclass 2: Music Production & Live Performance Topics
courses.content: The guest professor from the field of audio introduces industry-relevant, socially pertinent, and/or artistically current topics and insights. Emerging technologies, such as generative sound design, will also be covered.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to integrate knowledge of industry-relevant, socially pertinent, and/or artistically current topics into their concepts and creative work.

courses.title: Game Audio Directing & Analysis
courses.content: Expansion of non-linear work with sound in visual contexts and interaction Analysis of current non-linear sound concepts and their sound aesthetics Opportunities for developing a unique sound aesthetic in virtual, interactive systems Sound dramaturgy - sequences and processes in non-linear systems
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to work with the aesthetics of non-linear sound and interact within a visual context.

courses.title: Interactive Audio Environments & Interfaces 1
courses.content: Interactive Audio Environments Interfaces for sound control and user interaction Integration of middleware
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to integrate practical experience with current interactive audio environments into their work.

courses.title: Music Production Advanced 1
courses.content: Music composition und production advanced Mix & mastering advanced AI und machine learning mixing tools in music production Audio productions - practice and feedback
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop advanced strategies for mixing and mastering. They can also technically prepare music and stems for use in interactive audio systems.

courses.title: Non-linear Composition & Sound Design
courses.content: Specifics of composing in non-linear/interactive systems Sound aesthetics and compositional possibilities Mixing in real-time audio engines Sound design implementation Generative sound design Sound synthesis in interactive environments Control through interfaces Immersion Spatiality in real-time audio engines
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply advanced composition techniques in interactive systems. They can also apply advanced sound design as well as mixing and effects in interactive systems.

courses.title: Project Coaching Audio
courses.content: Detailed, subject-specific input for ongoing projects Creative input on current professional issues
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply their knowledge from the specialization in a subject- and project-oriented manner.

courses.title: Coaching & Reality Check 1
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Refinement Communication Design
courses.content: The ideas developed within the academic environment are compiled into compelling presentations and presented to various esteemed professionals and colleagues from the design industry. Feedback is gathered during these presentations.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to gain a nuanced perspective on their project ideas and solutions. They acquire and improve experience in presenting to a professional audience and enhance their ability to constructively use feedback in their design process.ely use feedback in their design process.

courses.title: Guest Professorship & Workshops 1 - Communication Design
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Refinement Communication Design
courses.content: Guest lecturers introduce relevant, socially pressing, and/or artistically current topics and ideas.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates gain insight into the respective field of work of the guest lecturers and are able to apply learned methods and processes to their own work.

courses.title: Interaction Design
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Refinement Communication Design
courses.content: Concepts and methods for designing user-friendly and/or experimental user interfaces, utilizing evaluation criteria and testing methods, as well as current scientific findings from interaction research (human-machine communication and relationship, interaction behavior, immersion and emotion, usability, intuitive operability, etc.).
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply advanced knowledge and skills in the conception and methodology of designing user-friendly and/or experimental user interfaces. They expertly implement the conception, design, and prototyping of innovative interfaces and forms of interaction, as well as information architecture with a visionary approach.

courses.title: Speculative Design
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Refinement Communication Design
courses.content: The topic of "Speculative Design" is introduced, and thought experiments and product ideas for fictional future scenarios are developed. The most well-known positions, theories, and examples of speculative design are presented and linked to practical exercises in creating innovative products. Through fictional future concepts, attention is drawn to current and anticipated issues in the world, encouraging reflection on possible ecological, economic, technological, political, or demographic scenarios.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates become familiar with design processes related to product development, with a special focus on ’what-if’ questions. They acquire competencies through developing project ideas, engage with political contexts, and reflect on their own social responsibility as designers.

courses.title: Transmedia Narratives
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Refinement Communication Design
courses.content: With the help of a specific semester project, a concept of transmedia storytelling is developed, in which a communicative message is told across multiple media. Design factors related to various narrative phenomena are explored and strategically aligned with media convergence.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to design narrative units and conceptualize a transmedia storytelling strategy upon completing the course. They utilize the synergistic effects of various media channels for their persuasive narrative.

courses.title: Art Direction and Film Design
courses.content: Advanced knowledge of common methods for implementing and optimizing design in both virtual and real spaces. Specific design skills in the conceptualization and realization of film and multimedia productions, as well as set design, in the context of multimedia (both virtual and real) and new technologies such as Virtual Production, Augmented Reality, and Virtual Reality. Art Direction and Film Design combine traditional techniques with digital possibilities, using the latest technological advancements and diverse digital platforms to design atmospheric environments where creative and exciting moving image communication takes place.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to acquire design skills to creatively shape a space, film set, or virtual scenery. They develop the ability to design visually and visionary, using digital tools to transfer this vision into a spatial or moving image project. Furthermore, they understand the differences in design across various platforms ’ from online, mobile, computers, and tablets to social media, web, and traditional media - as well as the connections between classic communication platforms such as theater, cinema, and television and the latest digital platforms such as gaming, augmented reality, and mobile (vertical format).

courses.title: CineCraft Transmedia Narrative 2
courses.content: Building on CineCraft Transmedia Narrative 1, students will deepen their skills in developing complex narrative structures that integrate various media formats. The focus is on transmedia and fusion formats such as film and games, as well as options like Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), and Extended Reality (XR). Participants will learn to develop deep characters and complex storylines while applying the latest technological developments, such as Virtual Production and AI-supported storytelling methods. Practical projects will encourage the integration of innovative storytelling techniques and the creation of immersive experiences. Expert skills in organizing and structuring a workflow for larger, interdisciplinary teams in a multimedia context.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to implement advanced cross-platform storytelling to seamlessly tell stories across various media and platforms. They develop cross-media narrative strategies to integrate multiple media formats and utilize AI-supported storytelling methods to enhance narrative development and improve efficiency. Furthermore, they integrate innovative media technologies to create immersive and cutting-edge narrative experiences.

courses.title: CineTech Innovations Masterclass 2
courses.content: Building on the foundation of Masterclass 1, with a focus on deeper exploration of technological advancements and innovative formats in filmmaking. Continuation and further development of projects from Masterclass 1 in new contexts.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop and implement the latest trends in film production technology. They integrate these trends into innovative formats and content and combine various disciplines with technology to create new forms of communication. Furthermore, they gain hands-on experience with the latest film production technologies, such as Virtual Production.

courses.title: CineTech Preproduction Mastery 2
courses.content: Building on the skills acquired in CineTech Preproduction Mastery 1, this course aims to enable participants to more effectively utilize modern technologies to develop complex, cross-platform stories and create immersive narrative experiences. The course builds on the use of new AI tools and digital technologies for creating previsualizations and innovative formats, deepening participants' knowledge and skills in applying these technologies for narrative development. The focus is on expanding classical storytelling structures towards cross-platform and cross-media storytelling, as well as on the previsualization and visual preproduction of more complex narrative structures and challenging cross-media formats.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to use advanced artificial intelligence to optimize character and plot development. They apply digital technologies proficiently to create previsualizations and innovative formats. Furthermore, they develop and integrate complex cross-platform stories and engage in cross-media storytelling by synchronizing narrative elements across various media formats. They can previsualize complex narrative structures through detailed previsualizations and visually preproduce challenging cross-media formats. In addition, they support and develop innovative storytelling formats while continuously updating their technological knowledge to adapt to the latest advancements in digital moving image production.

courses.title: DoP 2 Masterclass
courses.content: Consecutive to D.o.P 1 Masterclass ’ ongoing. Advanced analysis, optimization, integration, and problem-solving skills for handling complex lighting and camera-related challenges in intricate scenarios, project workflows, and operational options. Focused planning knowledge and execution skills in lighting and camera workflows using state-of-the-art technology. Refined artistic, aesthetic, and organizational skills in camera and lighting work across diverse genres in a cross-platform context. The emphasis is on using professional lighting and camera techniques for complex scenarios, especially in multimedia and special effects-heavy film productions.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to work confidently with digital cinematographic equipment. They shape their expertise in art history and artistic influences into a unique personal style. Furthermore, they master digital equipment to the extent that they can experiment artistically across platforms.

courses.title: Staging Masterclass
courses.content: Advanced knowledge and skills in working with actors using various acting techniques (e.g., Method Acting), as well as the ability to communicate personal ideas and visions to team members and actors, inspiring them for innovative, cinematic cross-media projects, and leading and directing them within larger production teams in multimedia and heterogeneous contexts. Specific competencies and skills for all aspects of realizing a large-scale, cross-platform multimedia production: staging visions or trends for creative content, integrating diverse team members in a large-scale digital moving image production, motivating them to achieve peak performance, handling creative content with precision and nuance, and directing it through to presentation on various platforms using advanced technology.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to carry out a production with a larger film team. They can work with actors using various techniques and recognize and apply different methods and approaches to acting. Furthermore, they lead, direct, and motivate all creative members of a film team. In addition, they are capable of staging complex concepts in space while successfully collaborating with highly specialized creatives.

courses.title: Creative Business: Financing
courses.content: The course addresses the various possibilities for financing creative projects and businesses in the creative industry, along with the associated challenges and risks. In the course, new and innovative financing methods such as crowdfunding, grants, and venture capital, as well as more traditional methods like loans and subsidies, will be introduced. Students will learn how to assess the feasibility of their projects and identify the best sources of financing for their needs. Furthermore, the course will cover the importance of financial management and controlling, as well as the role of human resources and decision-making in securing financing and running a successful creative business.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to identify the various possibilities for financing creative projects and businesses in the creative industry. They recognize the challenges and risks associated with different sources of financing and can assess the feasibility of their projects in order to determine the most suitable financing sources for their needs.

courses.title: Presentations & Pitching
courses.content: Within this course, various strategies and methods for impactful presentations in the creative industry are explored. The importance of preparation, storytelling, and feedback in creating powerful and memorable presentations will be discussed. In addition, students will learn how to apply these skills in the business world and understand the significance of effective pitching for their professional success. This course aims to equip students with valuable practical skills and knowledge that will help them succeed in the creative industry.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply and test various techniques and approaches for impactful presentations in the creative industry. They recognize the importance of careful preparation and use storytelling as a tool for creating memorable presentations. Furthermore, they can give and receive feedback to continuously improve their presentation skills. They apply the acquired skills and knowledge in real business environments and understand the relevance of effective pitching for their professional success in the creative industry. In doing so, they acquire valuable, practical skills that will support them in their professional careers.

courses.title: Production Management Methods 2
courses.content: This course on advanced methods of production management builds upon the foundational concepts covered in the previous course and delves deeper into the intricacies of project management. Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of advanced project management methods, including Scrum, Scrumban, Lean Six Sigma, event and campaign management. The course focuses on the practical application of these methods, as well as the tools and techniques used to manage complex production projects. In addition, students will learn about multi-project management and the challenges associated with managing multiple projects simultaneously. The course also prepares participants for the Scrum Product Owner certification exam. By the end, participants will have a solid understanding of advanced project management methods and be able to apply them effectively in real-world scenarios.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates acquire a comprehensive understanding of advanced project management methods and their practical application. They can assess the unique characteristics of a project and select the appropriate PM method for its management. Furthermore, they apply the tools and techniques of advanced project management to manage and monitor complex production projects. They understand the challenges associated with multi-project management and develop strategies to address them. In addition, they apply Scrum Product Owner principles and will be prepared for the Scrum Product Owner certification exam.

courses.title: Teambuilding & Leadership 1
courses.content: The aim of this course is to provide students with an understanding of the methods and challenges of team building and acquisition in the creative industry. Students will learn networking strategies, negotiation techniques, and the importance of empathy and responsibility in this process. The lecture also addresses collaboration and decision-making in team building, as well as the business relevance of building and maintaining a successful team.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates understand the importance of team building and acquisition in the creative industry. They apply networking strategies to recruit new team members and use negotiation techniques for effective team building. Furthermore, they recognize the significance of empathy and responsibility in the process of team building and acquisition. In addition, they gain an understanding of collaboration and decision-making processes that are essential for successful team building.

courses.title: Workflows & Pipelines
courses.content: The course "Workflows & Pipelines" provides students with an in-depth understanding of the various workflows and pipelines used in the creative industries. Students will learn about the different use cases of workflows and pipelines for projects of varying sizes and media formats. The lecture covers various methods for creating effective workflows and pipelines, including the tools and technologies used to manage and optimize project processes. Students will gain knowledge and skills in workflow management and collabora-tion, helping them improve their ability to work efficiently in teams and meet business demands.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates understand the various use cases for workflows and pipelines in the creative industry. They can evaluate and select appropriate workflow methods and tools based on project requirements. Furthermore, they are able to design and implement effective workflows and pipelines for projects of different sizes and media formats. They acquire practical skills in workflow management and collaboration, thereby improving their ability to work efficiently in teams. In addition, they develop a critical understanding of the business relevance of workflow management and the importance of delivering projects on time and within budget.

courses.title: Designed Experiences in Technology
courses.module: Compulsory Electives 3 - Electives - Designed Experiences in Technology
courses.content: This course focuses on the principles and techniques for creating immersive and interactive experiences using technology. Students will learn about immersion and interaction, principles of game design, virtual reality environments, and interactive spaces. They will explore successful case studies in the field of technology and the design strategies used to create these experiences. Additionally, students will engage with sound and music design, user testing and evaluation, as well as prototype development. By the end of the course, students will have developed a prototype of an immersive experience using technology and game design principles.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to understand the principles of designing immersive experiences using technology. They develop strategies for designing such experiences, including the use of technology and game design principles. Furthermore, they apply the fundamentals of game design, including mechanics, story, and player engagement. They analyze case studies of successfully designed technology experiences to examine the strategies used in creating them. In addition, they design virtual reality environments and interactive spaces, with a focus on the principles of immersive experience design.

courses.title: Generative Design
courses.content: Generative Design is a rule-based process in which mechanical devices, biological processes, computer programs, or other systems are used to generate designs. Algorithmic processes replace manual intervention. The creative effort lies in designing and implementing the rule sets, as well as evaluating the results. The historical background and pi-oneers of generative form creation (Buckminster Fuller, Otto Frei, and others) will be introduced in the introductory lecture block, followed by a brainstorming session where a shared vision is defined. The central part of the course is a multi-day workshop: over two or three intensive days, we will focus on the collaborative exploration of generative forms. Analog experiments will be conducted and translated into digital reproductions. Programming languages opti-mized for generative design in a live performance context will also be used, allowing new approaches even for those without prior programming experience. All participants contribute their unique skills to a multidisciplinary exploration of the subject. The intensive interpersonal collaboration during the workshop leads to new ideas and approaches, which will manifest in finished generative designs that will also be translated into sound forms. In the final part of the course, the results will be documented and presented.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates acquire historical knowledge about programmed art and programmed design. They are able to recreate significant milestones of generative form development using analog generative mechanisms (such as pendulums, soap bubble frames, etc.). Furthermore, they learn how to design such mechanisms themselves and build prototypes of them. They understand that there are IDEs and programming languages optimized for the specific requirements of generative design. In addition, they improve their ability to work in interdisciplinary teams.

courses.title: World Building for Fiction
courses.module: Compulsory Electives 3 - Electives - World Building for Fiction
courses.content: World Building for Fictional Worlds offers a comprehensive overview of techniques and tools for world-building, covering various aspects such as geography, history, mythology, culture, conflicts, storytelling, mythology and religion, as well as technical aspects. This course is designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to create realistic and believable fictional worlds. This includes map-making, climate and weather, culture and society, conflict and storytelling techniques, visual and audio design, as well as political and economic systems. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop unique and captivating fictional worlds that engage and excite their audience.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates gain an understanding of the fundamental concepts of world-building, such as geography, history, and mythology. They develop unique and believable cultures, religions, and social structures for their fictional worlds and design captivating characters that seamlessly fit into them. Furthermore, they are familiar with the technical aspects of world-building, such as map creation and applying visual and audio design. They collaborate effectively with other professional designers and create a coherent and immersive world that captivates their audience.

courses.title: Accompanying Seminar 1 Master Thesis
courses.content: In-depth knowledge and skills related to the Master's thesis: Independent handling of a complex, interdisciplinary problem based on scientific and methodological approaches, as well as competencies in presenting and discussing the developed research proposals.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to create a well-founded research proposal on the topic of their master’s thesis and acquire the ability to implement the chosen research method.

courses.title: Peer Presentation 2: Conference Reports
courses.content: In this course, students acquire the competence to make optimal use of conference experiences through a didactically sound approach. They learn how to maximize the benefits of conferences by building professional networks, attending keynote speeches, and participating in relevant workshops. After attending a conference, students are encouraged to share their insights in presentation events, which sharpens their ability to critically reflect and communicate complex ideas. The focus is on developing presentation skills and effectively conveying complex content to a broad audience. By integrat-ing research skills and the ability to summarize and present information precisely, students are empowered to enhance their academic and professional capabilities.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to build and maintain professional networks at conferences. They understand the value of keynotes, workshops, and sessions for expanding their knowledge and skills. Furthermore, they can conduct effective research, present complex ideas to broad audiences, and critically analyze conference topics. In doing so, they develop innovative solutions to real-world problems and enhance their academic and professional competence.

courses.title: Transfer Project 1
courses.content: Professionalized field-specific knowledge and skills in collaborating, implementing, and publishing multimedia or interdisciplinary practical tasks within the framework of multiple projects, through autonomous use of complex methods and techniques for independent learning and problemsolving, advanced self-organization, and outstanding justification and explanation competence regarding the creative, artistic, and interdisciplinary development and design process.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates work for 25 hours on a master’s project outside of their own, gaining exposure to different project cultures and styles.

courses.title: Master Project - Realisation - AUDIOVISUAL ENVIRONMENTS
courses.content: Input and implementation of audiovisual Master’s concepts using the latest technology during the production phase: musical and sound design for various applications, rang-ing from purely auditory to interactive, in the students’ Master projects / coaching. Project-specific exploration, possibilities of auditory and visual representation, standards and methods of interdisciplinary networking of objects, exploring technical solutions, transformation of processes through new tools, and incorporating new input from previous semesters.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply specific knowledge and skills in the realization of multimedia projects, focusing on high-quality and original design as well as technical problem-solving competence. Furthermore, they apply expert competencies to independently establish collaborations in interdisciplinary teams and to organize and reflect on group processes.

courses.title: Master Project - Realisation - COMMUNICATION DESIGN
courses.content: Based on the students' project ideas, subject-specific questions of communication design will be discussed. The focus is on the detailed development of strategies to achieve a communication goal, as well as the planning and organization for its implementation.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop concrete communication goals and strategies to achieve the formulated objectives and implement these strategies. Furthermore, they enhance their skills in defining their role as designers within the project.

courses.title: Master Project - Realisation - FILM
courses.content: Comprehensive knowledge of methods, workflows, and tools in Future Cinema, with a focus on innovation-oriented, cross-platform applications. Specific knowledge and skills in the realization of innovative Future Cinema projects, with an emphasis on high-quality and original design and technical problem-solving competence. Expert competencies in independently establishing collaboration within interdisciplinary teams and reflecting on or organizing group processes. Autonomous implementation of ambitious Future Cinema concepts using the latest technology during the production phase.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to work with a larger, complex, interdisciplinary team during the realization process of their work after the planning phase. They carry out the production phase, which seamlessly transitions into the post-production phase and finalization. Furthermore, they work on their project with professional guidance.

courses.title: Audio Masterclass 3: Music Production & Live Performance Topics
courses.content: The guest professor from the field of audio introduces industry-relevant, socially press-ing, and/or artistically current topics and ideas. (e.g., Emerging Technologies in 3D Audio & Immersive Audio Introduction).
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to develop an in-depth understanding of the selected area and critically reflect on it.

courses.title: Generative Sound & Visual Art
courses.content: Expansion of implementation competencies in the areas of: A/V Art, Visualization (e.g., Touch Designer / vvvv) Procedural Composing & Systems (e.g., MaxMsp): AI, Generative Audio Composition Art-Based Research
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to integrate the individual, master project-related expansion of their knowledge from one of the aforementioned specialized areas into their creative work.

courses.title: Guest Lecture - Generative Sound & Visual Art
courses.content: Guest Lecture - Emerging Technologies: Generative Sound Art Introduction & Concept Digital Arts and Visualization Media Reflection
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to understand generative artistic A/V works with a critical consideration of emerging technologies, algorithmic art, and AI, and to incorporate these insights into their own creative work.

courses.title: Interactive Audio Environments & Interfaces 2
courses.content: Interactive Audio Environments Interfaces for Sound Control and User Interaction VR Integration
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply practical experience in integrating current interactive studio environments and interfaces into their creative work for virtual reality installations and computer games.

courses.title: Music Production Advanced 2 - Sound & AI
courses.content: Music Composition and Production Advanced Mix & Mastering Advanced AI and Machine Learning Mixing Tools in Music Production Audio Production Practice and Feedback
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply advanced strategies for mixing and mastering. They can also prepare music and stems for use in interactive audio systems.

courses.title: Coaching & Reality Check 2
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Professionalization Communication Design
courses.content: Consecutive to C&R 1 from the 2nd semester: The ideas developed in the university environment are compiled into convincing presentations and presented to various respected personalities and work collectives in the design industry. Feedback is obtained in the process.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to gain a differentiated view of their project ideas and solution approaches. They gain experience in presenting in front of a specialized audience, improve their skills, and use feedback constructively for their design process.

courses.title: Data Visualization
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Professionalization Communication Design
courses.content: The subject of the course is the visualization of complex data, contexts and processes that relate to the examination of a specific project topic.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to utilize acquired competencies in data visualization to clearly present complex relationships. They make patterns visible and, where appropriate, interactively experienceable. Furthermore, they master conceptual and design challenges in visualizing datasets and formulating visual arguments.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Mass Communication
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Professionalization Communication Design
courses.content: Drafts for mass communication campaigns are developed based on a defined impact objective. The drafts are treated as hypotheses in the scientific sense and are tested for the desired effect using impact research methods from neighboring scientific disciplines.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply a theoretically sound repertoire of methods to review self-imposed performance targets.

courses.title: Guest Professorship & Workshops 2 - Communication Design
courses.module: Compulsory Elective 2 - Specialization Professionalization Communication Design
courses.content: Guest lecturers contribute relevant, socially virulent and/or artistically topical themes and impulses.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates gain an insight into the respective field of work of the guest lecturer and are able to apply the methods and processes they have learned to their own work.

courses.title: Guest Professorship & Workshops - Film
courses.content: The guest professor introduces current topics and insights from the film industry and emerging technologies, drawing from their own cutting-edge work. The covered topics are closely related to or in dialogue with the detailed concept of the multimedia project. Engaging with the established expert challenges students professionally and methodologically, as well as in their personal development, particularly in the context of integrating new technology into film and media production.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply expanded content-related and technological perspectives to their chosen field. They can implement the content shared by the guest professor into their project work and recognize the broader connections of artistic creation and articulate them effectively.

courses.title: Postproduction Masterclass
courses.content: The focus is on the comprehensive acquisition and refinement of technical skills and creative work using advanced post-production software (such as Avid or DaVinci) in the field of moving images, including its various genres and forms. It is essential to create a synthesis between art historical education, technical expertise in handling state-of-the-art hardware and software, and a profound understanding of the narrative aspects of film. This serves the purpose of fully grasping and supporting the intentions of the work and the artistic ambitions of the directors and writers. Moreover, students engage in digital, virtual spheres to apply and test the aforementioned knowledge and skills in an expanded context.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates acquire a deep understanding of the impact of color and editing. They apply their artistic knowledge in an interdisciplinary and cross-platform manner and are familiar with the relevant software and hardware (e.g., DaVinci Resolve, Avid Media Composer) to effectively utilize their skills. Furthermore, they understand the importance of editing on perception and narrative flow.

courses.title: Creative Business: Models & Methods
courses.content: This course provides an overview of various creative business models and methods used in the creative industries. Students will learn about different models for monetizing creative work, such as subscription models, freemium models and pay-what-you-want models. They will also learn about innovative methods for developing and launching new products and services, including design thinking, lean startup and agile development methods. Using case studies and examples, students will gain insight into how creative companies can apply these models and methods to succeed in a competitive marketplace.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to describe different business models used in the creative industries and assess the strengths and weaknesses of these models for creative enterprises. They apply design thinking and lean start-up methods to develop new products and services. Furthermore, they are able to identify the most important success factors for founding a creative company and evaluate the business potential of creative ideas.

courses.title: Guest Professorship, Workshops & Excursion - Producing
courses.content: This guest workshop covers current topics in the production and creative industries, including conceptualization, financing, budgeting and project management. Students have the opportunity to talk to interesting personalities who are successful in the industry.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to identify and analyze the different roles and responsibilities of producers in the creative industries. They develop critical thinking skills to assess the feasibility and marketability of a creative project. Furthermore, they can assess the impact of new technologies on the production process and the creative industries as a whole.

courses.title: Marketing & Dissemination
courses.content: Marketing and dissemination of creative works is crucial to their success and profitability. In this course, students will gain an overview of marketing methods and strategies for the creative industry, including challenges and success criteria. Students will learn about market analysis, branding, advertising, public relations and social media marketing, as well as the importance of effective storytelling and content creation for successful marketing campaigns. The course also looks at the distribution of creative works through various channels, including traditional and digital media, festivals and exhibitions. By the end of the course, students will have a comprehensive understanding of the complex processes involved in marketing and distribution in the creative industries.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to apply marketing methods and strategies in the creative industry, conduct market analyses, and develop branding strategies. They plan and implement advertising, public relations, and social media campaigns, use storytelling and content creation, and employ various distribution channels. In doing so, they apply a comprehensive understanding of marketing and dissemination processes in practice.

courses.title: Media Law 2
courses.content: Building on the basic knowledge acquired in the Media Law 1 course, this advanced course offers students an in-depth examination of the legal landscape of the media industry. The course looks at the legal principles and regulations that govern distribution, monetization and new technologies such as cryptocurrencies, blockchain and digital platforms. Students will examine the legal frameworks that apply to various media platforms, including television, streaming services, social media and games. In addition, students will learn about the complex legal issues that arise in the production and distribution of media content, such as advertising regulations, data protection laws and claims for damages for copyright infringement.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to analyze and evaluate the legal framework for the media industry, including traditional platforms such as television and new technologies such as blockchain and cryptocurrencies. They apply legal principles to real-world scenarios such as the production and distribution of media content and understand the impact of legal decisions on the media industry. Furthermore, they develop critical thinking skills to assess the impact of legal regulations and evaluate principles regarding the monetization strategies of the media industry, including advertising regulations and intellectual property rights.

courses.title: Teambuilding & Leadership 2
courses.content: This course builds on the concepts covered in the previous course and provides students with a deeper understanding of the challenges and opportunities associated with leading and managing teams in different contexts. The course looks at key leadership methods and approaches that are effective in motivating and engaging team members, including building a positive organizational culture, managing remote teams and promoting diversity and inclusion. Participants will also learn about the importance of retention management and employer branding for attracting and retaining talent. By the end of the course, students will have a comprehensive understanding of the complex processes involved in fostering and managing teams in the creative industries.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates understand the key leadership methods and approaches that are effective in motivating and retaining team members. They are able to apply retention strategies to keep top talent, recognize the importance of diversity and inclusion in team leadership, and effectively manage remote teams in virtual environments. In addition, they develop employer branding strategies to attract and retain top talent for their organization.

courses.title: Dramaturgy & Multiplatform Storytelling
courses.module: Compulsory Electives 3 - Electives - Dramaturgy & Multiplatform Storytelling
courses.content: The course builds on the fundamental principles of dramaturgy and applies these principles to various media and platforms. Participants will learn the principles of creating compelling stories tailored to specific target audiences and platforms and how to effectively implement these stories on digital and analog platforms. An understanding of the unique characteristics of different platforms will be developed. Insights into the development of stories optimized for specific platforms will be provided, and the importance of genre conventions and audience expectations in crafting effective stories will be emphasized. The course will explore the implementation of stories on digital platforms, along with the unique challenges and opportunities they present (such as the internet, mobile phones, tablets, social media, games, VR, AR). Students will be introduced to the development of stories optimized for digital platforms, including interactive storytelling and transmedia storytelling. They will also learn about the importance of user experience in developing effective stories for digital platforms, including immersive experiences and location-based installations.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to analyze and critique the implementation of stories across various media and platforms. They apply the principles of dramaturgy to their own creative projects on different platforms and media and collaborate effectively with other creatives to develop and refine stories across various media. Furthermore, they understand the importance of consistency and coherence across multiple platforms and media. They develop techniques for refining and improving stories and are able to effectively implement narratives across diverse media formats and platforms.

courses.title: Performance & Interaction
courses.content: The course Performance & Interaction aims to explore and experience participatory principles in audiovisual art, as well as interaction possibilities and interfaces for the audience or individual participants within (A/V) performances, installations, or generally narrative structures from different perspectives. It also questions how interactive processes alter the content and meaning of ephemeral narratives. Furthermore, it addresses how various media influence and interact with each other, and the search for using interactions for new forms of expression within current technologies. The ILV covers a range of topics, including a brief overview and reflection on well-known performance practices, the use of technology in contemporary performances, audience engagement, and ethical considerations regarding the use of technology in performances (key point: "accessibility"). Through lectures, discussions, and practical exercises such as "prototyping," new ideas and approaches will be developed that can be applied in the students' projects. Students are encouraged to experiment with various forms of current technologies, including audio and video equipment, interactive installations, and digital interfaces.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to critically reflect on and experiment with participatory processes, interactions, and related technologies in live performances. They also work with various performance technologies, practices, and media to create innovative, engaging, and reflective performances.

courses.title: Accompanying Seminar 2 Master Thesis
courses.content: In-depth engagement with the chosen topics of the Master's theses. Independent handling of the complex, interdisciplinary problem based on scientific methodology, which is critically reflected upon, discussed, and supported in the seminar.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are able to create a research proposal with a scientific question and acquire the knowledge required for writing their master’s thesis. They can transform their individual theoretical engagement into a written scientific work and develop it into a publishable form.

courses.title: Guest lectures
courses.content: Expanding knowledge in selected topics of current research and design practice, such as the expansion of themes in multimedia art, audio cultures, design theory and research, current design principles, aesthetics, semiotics, game theory, and state-of-the-art technological developments.
